title: RBAC & Auditlog Evidence Automation — Auditor Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational cheat-sheet for preparing RBAC v2 audit log evidence for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 assessments and for use during auditor interviews. It focuses on the intersection of RBAC changes, the audit log schema, automated evidence extraction to the SIEM, and common auditor Q&A.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, compliance owners, SRE/oncall, platform engineers building log exports, and solutions engineers who support enterprise customers.
- Scope: RBAC v2 events (role grants/revokes, role definition changes, policy updates), authentication/authorization lifecycle traces, SIEM export transformations, and the automated evidence pipeline used during attestations.

Quick summary of the evidence flow (1-liner):
RBAC change -> internal API event -> producer logs (structured JSON) -> log router (transform/enrich) -> SIEM ingest (index + parsers) -> evidence snapshots archived -> auditor queries and runbook.

Key log fields to preserve (audit-quality):
- timestamp_iso: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (e.g., 2024-10-21T18:12:03Z)
- event_id: UUID v4
- actor_id: internal user id / service account id
- actor_display_name: human-readable name (for UI corroboration)
- actor_principals: [oauth_client_id, session_id] (list)
- action: canonical verb (role.assign, role.remove, role.define, policy.update, login.success, login.failure)
- resource_type: role | policy | user | service-account
- resource_id: canonical resource id (role:roles/{id})
- prev_state_hash: SHA256 snapshot hash (optional but preferred)
- diff_summary: small human-readable diff for role/policy changes
- request_id: request tracing id tying API call to job/workflow
- ip_address: optional where relevant for user-initiated changes
- result: success | failure | partial
- audit_context: {ticket: string, change_request: string} (if available)
- provenance: producer_service, version, environment

Why these fields matter: preserves non-reputable link between action, actor, and change; prev_state_hash enables snapshot verification; request_id ties logs to traces and replay.

SIEM ingestion & parsers (practical guidance):
- Keep original structured JSON in a raw/raw_json field; do not flatten away core fields.
- Standardize timestamp to @timestamp (UTC) at ingestion time and retain timestamp_iso as original string.
- Implement a parser that maps 'action' to standardized control events used in the control matrix (e.g., map role.assign -> AC-2.2 create; role.remove -> AC-2.3 revoke).
- Add ingestion tags: environment:prod|staging, pipeline:rbac-v2, schema_version:1.2.
- Configure SIEM to keep a 1:1 relation between event_id and index entry; no deduplication during initial ingest.

Automated evidence snapshot runbook (high-level steps):
1) Trigger: control owner requests snapshot via internal tooling (UI or /api/v1/evidence/snapshot).
2) Query: snapshot job runs the canonical SIEM query for control (stored query id) with time range and optional ticket id.
3) Export: raw JSON results + parsed CSV summary saved to secure artifact bucket (immutable manifest with checksum).
4) Provenance: snapshot manifest includes git sha of parser/transforms, schema_version, snapshot_trigger_id, operator.
5) Archive: evidence packaged into auditor zip with README that maps items to SOC 2 / ISO control IDs.

Sample SIEM queries (conceptual) to reproduce evidence: (adjust to your SIEM language)
- Show all role assignment events for last 90 days: pipeline:rbac-v2 AND action:role.assign | sort timestamp desc
- Changes to admin role definition: resource_type:role AND resource_id:roles/admin AND action:policy.update | include diff_summary, prev_state_hash
- Failed authorization attempts following role changes: actor_id:(list) AND action:authorization.failure AND timestamp > {role_change_ts}

Control mapping excerpt (example rows, keep as text here):
- SOC 2 CC6 (Access Controls): role.assign, role.remove, policy.update -> evidence: SIEM index + snapshot of role definitions + change diffs + approval ticket link.
- ISO 27001 A.9.2.3 (Management of privileged access rights): role.assign (grant), role.remove (revoke) -> evidence: assignment log, approver id, approval ticket, periodic review log.
- ISO 27001 A.12.4 (Logging and monitoring): authentication/login.success & login.failure -> evidence: retention policy, parser rules, SIEM retention proof.

Gap analysis summary (current known gaps and mitigations):
- Gap: approvals are captured in a separate ticketing system but not always linked in audit_context; many manual matches during audits.
  Mitigation: prioritize SEC-842 (Jira) to add ticket id to request headers and require ticket for role changes in UI.
- Gap: prev_state snapshots are not recorded for policy updates older than schema_version 1.0.
  Mitigation: backfill important changes via DB snapshots for last 12 months; enforce prev_state_hash going forward.
- Gap: service-to-service role changes (automation) sometimes use a service account without operator context.
  Mitigation: require a justification field and operator wrapper for automation workflows; annotate actor_principals with orchestration_job_id.

Common auditor Q&A + suggested answers (prep):
Q: How do you prove that the person who changed a role was authorized?
A: We provide the role.assign event (event_id + timestamp), the actor_id and actor_display_name, the approval ticket captured in audit_context.ticket (link to JIRA), and the approval log from our ticketing system. If the change was automated, we provide orchestration_job_id and the responsible service owner.

Q: What prevents log tampering?
A: Logs are forwarded immediately to the SIEM (immutable index policy), the ingestion manifests are checksum-signed and archived to an immutable object store. We retain raw payloads and keep a copy of the original raw_json in a WORM bucket for the retention window.

Q: How do you reconcile a role definition to the UI displayed permissions?
A: We include a snapshot of the role definition (role:{id} JSON) in the evidence package and a prev_state_hash that maps to the stored configuration in the config-repo (git SHA). Console screenshots can be added where required.

Q: How long are logs retained and how is retention enforced?
A: Production RBAC logs are retained in the SIEM for 3 years (index policy) and archived to cold storage per our retention schedule. Retention policies are enforced via lifecycle policies and periodic retention audits (audit job id included in manifests).

Operational playbook for an auditor session (step-by-step):
1) Receive auditor scope and required control IDs.
2) Run stored SIEM queries for each control (provide preview and raw JSON snapshots).
3) Generate evidence.zip using snapshot API and send SFTP link to auditor (or upload to approved portal).
4) Provide live walkthrough: show event -> link to ticket -> show approval -> show manifest checksum -> show snapshot archive.
5) Flag items where manual reconciliation was necessary (list in the README).

Open questions / decisions for roadmap: (for product and infra)
- Enforce ticket-id requirement on role change UI? (SEC-842)
- Mandatory prev_state_hash for all policy change events? (Yes recommended)
- Add dedupe-proof cryptographic signing of event batches at producer level? (architectural tradeoff)

Action items (owner / ETA):
- SEC-842: Add ticket-id header enforcement and UI validation (owner: Miguel Ortega, ETA: 2024-12-06).
- SEC-870: Backfill prev_state snapshots for critical roles (owner: Sophie Kim, ETA: 2025-01-15).
- Add parser version check to snapshot manifest (owner: Jordan Lee, ETA: 2024-11-20).

Appendix: quick checklist for evidence zips (for control owner to verify before sending):
- [ ] Raw JSON export included (raw_json.ndjson)
- [ ] Parsed CSV summary included (summary.csv)
- [ ] Snapshot manifest (manifest.json) with checksums and parser git sha
- [ ] Mapping doc linking files to SOC 2 / ISO controls (mapping.md)
- [ ] Approval ticket snapshots (ticket_{id}.pdf or ticket_links.txt)
- [ ] Role definition JSONs referenced (role_{id}.json)
- [ ] README with steps to reproduce queries in SIEM and supporting links

Notes to self / things I jotted down during the last auditor dry-run:
- Auditors asked for an explanation of how we handle automated/CI-driven role changes -> prepare short explainer and recorded screen demo.
- Keep a pre-approved SFTP endpoint and checklist to reduce back-and-forth during live sessions.

If you are preparing for an auditor session and want me to generate the snapshot for a given control id and date range, drop the control id and range in #sec-audit on Slack or open Jira SEC-842 and tag me.

End of cheatsheet.
